title: Read how a run ended

blocks.text: A port's berth-allocation MILP feeds a dashboard that shows one badge per run. The team wants the badge to answer two questions before anyone looks at the numbers: is there a plan to use, and could more search still change the answer?
Write `verdict(termination)` in `verdict.py`. `termination` is a `mathopt.Termination`, the `termination` field of a `SolveResult`. Return a dict with three keys:

items: `"has_plan"`: `True` when the reason is `OPTIMAL` or `FEASIBLE`, and `False` for any other reason.
`"settled"`: `True` when the reason is `OPTIMAL` (the bounds are within the gap tolerances, even if they are not equal) or `INFEASIBLE` (no plan exists), and `False` for any other reason.
`"limit"`: the name of `termination.limit` (`"TIME"`, `"NODE"`, `"SOLUTION"`, `"UNDETERMINED"`, ...) when the reason is `FEASIBLE` or `NO_SOLUTION_FOUND`, and `None` for any other reason.

blocks.text: A `Limit` member's name is its `.name` attribute: `mathopt.Limit.NODE.name` is `"NODE"`. Read the reason from `termination.reason` and compare it with the members of `mathopt.TerminationReason`.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

R = mathopt.TerminationReason


def verdict(termination: mathopt.Termination) -> dict:
    """Is there a plan, is the answer settled, and which limit stopped the run?"""
    reason = termination.reason
    has_plan = reason in (R.OPTIMAL, R.FEASIBLE)
    settled = reason in (R.OPTIMAL, R.INFEASIBLE)
    limit = None
    if reason in (R.FEASIBLE, R.NO_SOLUTION_FOUND) and termination.limit is not None:
        limit = termination.limit.name
    return {"has_plan": has_plan, "settled": settled, "limit": limit}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    stopped = mathopt.Termination(reason=R.FEASIBLE, limit=mathopt.Limit.TIME,
                                  objective_bounds=mathopt.ObjectiveBounds(primal_bound=90.0, dual_bound=100.0))
    print(verdict(stopped))

cases.says: an OPTIMAL run has a plan, is settled, and names no limit
a FEASIBLE run stopped on a node limit has a plan, is not settled, and names NODE
NO_SOLUTION_FOUND on a time limit has no plan, is not settled, and names TIME
an INFEASIBLE run has no plan and is settled, since no plan exists
an OPTIMAL run whose bounds differ, stopped by a gap tolerance, is still settled
a FEASIBLE run whose solver did not say which limit names UNDETERMINED, not TIME

origin.section: A Gap Stop Ends OPTIMAL; Every Other Limit Ends FEASIBLE or NO_SOLUTION_FOUND

concepts: OPTIMAL and INFEASIBLE are settled, FEASIBLE holds an unproven plan, NO_SOLUTION_FOUND holds none, and termination.limit names the limit or UNDETERMINED
